title: In Massachusetts the emergency situation is itself the ePrescribing exception
subtopic: Emergency situation definition and its follow-up route
rule_summary: 105 CMR 721.010 defines an EMERGENCY SITUATION as (1) situations in which the prescribing practitioner intends to prescribe a controlled substance the IMMEDIATE ADMINISTRATION of which is necessary for the proper treatment of the intended ultimate user, AND EITHER (a) it is not reasonably possible for the practitioner to generate or transmit an ELECTRONIC PRESCRIPTION prior to the dispensing, OR (b) the practitioner determines the Electronic Prescription requirement would result in a DELAY THAT WOULD ADVERSELY IMPACT the patient's medical condition; or (2) any other Emergency Situation defined in Department guidance by the Commissioner under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 17. Under 105 CMR 721.020(A) every Prescription generated in the Commonwealth must be an Electronic Prescription unless it is issued under a 105 CMR 721.070 exception, and 105 CMR 721.070(A)(4) ENUMERATES 'Prescriptions issued or dispensed in Emergency Situations in accordance with 105 CMR 721.060' as exactly such an exception. A lawful Massachusetts emergency oral prescription is therefore ALWAYS issued under an ePrescribing exception, which is why 105 CMR 721.060(A) routes it to 105 CMR 721.070(B) for its follow-up rather than to the M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 20(c) two-day electronic default.
exam_relevance: Tests the step that decides which follow-up period applies. Massachusetts states a two-day electronic follow-up for oral prescriptions generally and a seven-business-day follow-up under the ePrescribing exceptions; the emergency pathway sits in the second because the emergency is the exception.

authority.name: Electronic prescription required unless an exception applies
Emergency situations enumerated as an ePrescribing exception

exceptions: Unlike 105 CMR 721.070(A)(3), the emergency exception is not applied for and held; it attaches to the situation itself.
The Commissioner may define further emergency situations in Department guidance under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 17.
common_confusions: Applying the M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 20(c) two-day electronic follow-up to an emergency oral prescription. The prescription is issued under the 105 CMR 721.070(A)(4) ePrescribing exception, and 105 CMR 721.060(A) directs it to 105 CMR 721.070(B) for its follow-up, so the two-day default is not the route it travels.
Reading the Massachusetts definition as carrying the federal no-appropriate-alternative-treatment element, which it does not.
Missing that the Massachusetts test is keyed to the impossibility or delay of an ELECTRONIC prescription, where the federal test is keyed to a WRITTEN one.
